question: In the opening verse of Obadiah, what specific proclamation and summons is delivered by an ambassador sent from the LORD among the heathen concerning Edom?
opt1: "Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle"
opt2: "Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make his paths straight"
opt3: "Proclaim ye this among the Gentiles; Prepare war, wake up the mighty men"
opt4: "Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired"
correct: "Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle"
explanation: Obadiah records the divine report and mobilization against Edom. Obadiah 1:1 (KJV) - "The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the LORD, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle."

question: According to Obadiah, what deceptive pride characterized Edom due to its mountain strongholds, and what does the LORD declare regarding their loftiness?
opt1: They trusted in their vast cavalry and iron chariots, yet the LORD declared their horses would stumble in rocky valleys
opt2: They dwelt in the clefts of the rock boasting no one could bring them down, yet the LORD would bring them down even if they nested among the stars
opt3: They built impenetrable walls of bronze around Bozrah, yet the LORD declared consuming fire would devour their palaces
opt4: They relied on secret underground cisterns and gold, yet the LORD proclaimed their wells would dry up and their silver be cursed
correct: They dwelt in the clefts of the rock boasting no one could bring them down, yet the LORD would bring them down even if they nested among the stars
explanation: Edom's cliff-dwelling fortifications in Mount Seir bred false security and pride. Obadiah 1:3-4 (KJV) - "The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground? Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the LORD."

question: How does Obadiah rhetorically contrast the complete plundering of Esau with the customary behavior of nocturnal thieves and grapegatherers?
opt1: Thieves leave the foundations intact and grapegatherers spare the tender shoots, whereas Edom's vineyards are entirely uprooted and burned
opt2: Robbers spare women and children while vintagers tithe the firstfruits, but Edom's allies slaughter both old and young without pity
opt3: Thieves steal only until they have enough and grapegatherers leave gleanings, but Esau's hidden treasures are totally searched out and stripped
opt4: Thieves work only by night and vintagers by day, whereas Edom's destruction arrives simultaneously in broad daylight and darkness
correct: Thieves steal only until they have enough and grapegatherers leave gleanings, but Esau's hidden treasures are totally searched out and stripped
explanation: The destruction of Edom is total, far exceeding the partial taking of common plunderers or harvesters. Obadiah 1:5-6 (KJV) - "If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes? How are the things of Esau searched out! how are his hidden things sought up!"

question: In Obadiah 1:7, what treacherous betrayal by Edom's confederates and peaceful allies is prophesied to bring about their downfall?
opt1: Their allied mercenaries poisoned their municipal water cisterns and opened Bozrah's city gates to foreign armies
opt2: Their covenant partners demanded triple tribute in silver and sold Edomite children as slaves to the Grecians
opt3: Their neighboring kings broke treaty oaths during the new moon and burned Edom's border towers to the ground
opt4: Those who ate their bread deceived them, brought them to the border, and laid a wound under them despite their lack of discernment
correct: Those who ate their bread deceived them, brought them to the border, and laid a wound under them despite their lack of discernment
explanation: Edom was undone from within by trusted treaty partners. Obadiah 1:7 (KJV) - "All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee; they that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee: there is none understanding in him."

question: What two renowned assets of Edom and Teman does the LORD specifically decree to destroy and dismay so that everyone of Mount Esau is cut off by slaughter?
opt1: The renowned wise men possessing understanding, and the formidable mighty men of Teman
opt2: The fortified watchtowers of Petra, and the wealthy merchant caravans traveling through Arabah
opt3: The ancient royal lineage of the dukes of Esau, and the sacrificial priesthood of Chemosh
opt4: The rich copper mines of Punon, and the elite archers defending the heights of Sela
correct: The renowned wise men possessing understanding, and the formidable mighty men of Teman
explanation: Edom, famed in antiquity for sages and warriors, would see both intellect and military strength dismantled. Obadiah 1:8-9 (KJV) - "Shall I not in that day, saith the LORD, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau? And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter."

question: What fundamental relational betrayal brings everlasting shame and destruction upon Edom when Jerusalem was invaded by strangers?
opt1: Refusing water and passage through the King's Highway when Moses led the tribes through the wilderness of Zin
opt2: Violence against their brother Jacob, standing aloof and acting as one of the foreign invaders when lots were cast upon Jerusalem
opt3: Melting down the sacred vessels of the temple to cast silver idols and altars dedicated to Baal-peor
opt4: Forming an offensive military coalition with Sennacherib of Assyria against King Hezekiah of Judah
correct: Violence against their brother Jacob, standing aloof and acting as one of the foreign invaders when lots were cast upon Jerusalem
explanation: The fraternal bond between Esau and Jacob intensified Edom's guilt during Jerusalem's fall. Obadiah 1:10-11 (KJV) - "For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever. In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them."

question: Among the eight prohibitions in Obadiah 1:12-14, what active, ruthless hostility did Edom execute against Judah's surviving fugitives in the day of distress?
opt1: They set fire to the remaining olive orchards and salted the agricultural fields around Bethlehem
opt2: They blinded the captured nobles of Judah and paraded them through the public squares of Teman
opt3: They stood in the crossway to cut off those escaping and delivered up the survivors to their captors
opt4: They pursued the high priest into the wilderness cave and plundered the ark of the covenant
correct: They stood in the crossway to cut off those escaping and delivered up the survivors to their captors
explanation: Edom actively blocked escape routes to intercept and hand over helpless Judean refugees. Obadiah 1:14 (KJV) - "Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress."

question: What divine principle of retributive justice (lex talionis) is pronounced against Edom and all heathen in the approaching Day of the LORD?
opt1: "An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth, until all the nations of the earth learn righteousness"
opt2: "Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed, for in the image of God made he man"
opt3: "Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord, and their foot shall slide in due time"
opt4: "As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head"
correct: "As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head"
explanation: God's righteous judgment precisely mirrors Edom's treacherous actions against Judah. Obadiah 1:15 (KJV) - "For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head."

question: In the prophetic restoration of Mount Zion, what vivid metaphors depict the victorious houses of Jacob and Joseph versus the house of Esau?
opt1: The house of Jacob as a fire and Joseph as a flame devouring the house of Esau as stubble until no remnant remains
opt2: The house of Jacob as a soaring eagle and Joseph as a lion tearing the house of Esau as a helpless gazelle
opt3: The house of Jacob as an overflowing river and Joseph as a storm washing away the house of Esau as shifting dust
opt4: The house of Jacob as an iron hammer and Joseph as an anvil crushing the house of Esau as brittle clay
correct: The house of Jacob as a fire and Joseph as a flame devouring the house of Esau as stubble until no remnant remains
explanation: Zion experiences deliverance and holiness while Jacob and Joseph consume Esau completely. Obadiah 1:17-18 (KJV) - "But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions. And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the LORD hath spoken it."

question: With what glorious theological climax and governance proclamation does the Book of Obadiah conclude in verse 21?
opt1: "And the LORD shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one LORD, and his name one"
opt2: "And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD's"
opt3: "For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea"
opt4: "The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah"
correct: "And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD's"
explanation: The prophecy concludes with the establishment of divine sovereignty and rule from Mount Zion. Obadiah 1:21 (KJV) - "And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the LORD's."
